record.paper_title: Open problems and some results on strongly closed subalgebras of B(X)
record.original_question: Let X be a complex locally convex topological vector space and let A be a complex algebra. A representation T of A on X is irreducible when no proper closed subspace of X is invariant under all representing operators T_a; it is n-fold irreducible when every n-tuple of linearly independent vectors has dense orbit in X^n under the diagonal action; and it is totally irreducible when it is n-fold irreducible for every natural number n. If T is irreducible and its commutant {S in L(X): S T_a = T_a S for every a in A} consists only of scalar multiples of the identity operator, must T be totally irreducible?

evidence.quote: A representation T is said to be totally irreducible, if it is n -fold irreducible for all n .
Does it follow that T is totally irreducible?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a complex locally convex topological vector space, let $A$ be a complex algebra, and let $T\colon A \to L(X)$ be a representation of $A$ on $X$, where $L(X)$ denotes the algebra of continuous linear operators on $X$. Write $T_a$ for the operator representing $a\in A$.

Call $T$:
- irreducible if there is no proper closed subspace $Y\subsetneq X$ with $T_a(Y)\subseteq Y$ for all $a\in A$;
- $n$-fold irreducible if for every $n$-tuple $(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ of linearly independent vectors in $X$, the orbit $\{(T_a x_1,\dots,T_a x_n) : a\in A\}$ is dense in $X^n$ (in the product topology);
- totally irreducible if $T$ is $n$-fold irreducible for every positive integer $n$.

The commutant of $T$ is $\{S\in L(X) : ST_a = T_a S \text{ for all } a\in A\}$.

Question: If $T$ is irreducible and its commutant consists only of scalar multiples of the identity operator on $X$, must $T$ be totally irreducible?
artifact.status_search_result: The question, posed by Fell and Doran, is known to be open in full generality for representations on arbitrary complex locally convex spaces. Partial affirmative results are known: for instance, Żelazko (Studia Mathematica, 1998) proved that on the F-space (s) and more generally on infinite topological products of the scalar field, every irreducible representation with trivial (scalar) commutant is totally irreducible. No general resolution for arbitrary locally convex X appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: A density theorem for algebra representations on the space (s)
status_evidence.snippet: An arbitrary irreducible representation of a real or complex algebra on the F-space (s), or more generally on an arbitrary infinite topological product of the field of scalars, is totally irreducible provided its commutant is trivial, which provides an affirmative solution to a problem of Fell and Doran for representations on these spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Affirmative answer is known in the special case of representations on (s) and on infinite products of the scalar field; the question is attributed to Fell and Doran.
